issues.title: Bloom filter for hash joins whose build side is a DELIM_GET
issues.hypothesis: In q17 the decorrelated subquery joins lineitem (60M rows, no filter) against DELIM_GET (2,001 distinct p_partkey values, condition l_partkey = p_partkey, COMPARE_EQUAL). The profile (json, current best) shows that SEQ_SCAN emitting 59,986,032 rows and that HASH_JOIN costing 0.47-0.53s CPU while producing only 59,686 rows. That join gets only the zonemap-only OptionalFilter key-set ranges and no Bloom filter. lineitem is ordered by orderkey, so the zonemap prunes nothing. The cause is in join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp (around line 331): when the RHS is a LOGICAL_DELIM_GET, build_side_has_filter = IsFiltering(join.children[0]), which tests the PROBE side (the bare lineitem scan) and gives false. CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:888) then refuses the BF. A DELIM_GET holds the distinct correlated values of the outer query, which is almost always a small, filtered subset of the probe domain. A previous run landed a similar 'BF with DELIM_GET build' change and measured q21 -4..-7.5%. With the BF, the subquery-side scan should go from 60M to about 0.4M rows (2,001 keys, hashed BF with about 0.5% false positives, as the outer scan already shows: 368K rows), and the 0.5s CPU hash-join probe mostly disappears.
issues.plan: 1) In src/optimizer/join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp, in the block `if (rhs_child->type == LogicalOperatorType::LOGICAL_DELIM_GET)`, set build_side_has_filter = true, or `IsFiltering(join.children[0]) || true-ish` guarded by the estimate: rhs estimated_cardinality < probe estimated_cardinality. The runtime checks still apply: CanUseBloomFilter requires probe estimate > ht->Count(), and SelectivityOptionalFilter (BF_THRESHOLD/BF_CHECK_N) switches the BF off if it is not selective. 2) Read IsFiltering and the comment there first, so you know why upstream picked children[0]. If DELIM_GET also shows up as the build of LEFT/MARK/SEMI joins, keep the existing join-type restrictions of the BF path unchanged. 3) Verify on q17: EXPLAIN ANALYZE should show 'IN BF' on the second lineitem scan and its row count dropping from 60M to under 1M. Check that results match with SET disabled_optimizers='join_filter_pushdown'. Also run the q02/q20/q22/q04 style correlated subqueries (EXISTS / scalar subqueries with DELIM) and compare results against the disabled-pushdown run. Use dbe-tool sql with several statements to get in-process A/B timings.
issues.expected_gain: q17 -5..-12% (removes about 0.45s of a hash-join probe on 60M rows); q02 possibly a few %; hidden correlated-subquery templates (q20, q21, q22-like) a few % each
issues.generality: Any decorrelated correlated subquery (scalar aggregate, EXISTS/NOT EXISTS lowered to DELIM joins) where the subquery scans a large table keyed on the correlated column, which is a very common analytical pattern. It could be slower when the delim set is huge and covers the whole domain (BF build plus probe cost with no pruning); the SelectivityOptionalFilter self-disable limits that to the first few vectors.
issues.risk: Low-medium. It only enables an existing, tested mechanism (BF) in one more case, and the BF can only drop rows that have no match. Watch out for NULL handling if the condition is IS NOT DISTINCT FROM (PushBloomFilter already lets NULLs pass when NullValuesAreEqual), and for MARK/ANTI joins, where filtering the probe side would be wrong: keep the existing join-type gating.
